items.headline: Yemeni government forces claim capture of Bab al-Mandeb strait and Mocha port from Houthis
items.summary: Yemen's internationally recognised government said Monday its forces had seized control of the Bab al-Mandeb strait, the Dhubab coastal district overlooking it, and the port city of Mocha, with a Saudi-led coalition flying roughly 100 jets in round-the-clock air support and striking 324 "high-value" Houthi targets in an offensive dubbed "Yemen Dawn." The Houthis disputed the claims, and hundreds of their fighters were reportedly surrounded near Dhubab, with some fleeing by boat.
items.actionable: A second chokepoint now contested on top of Hormuz keeps the safe-haven/shipping-risk premium underpinning gold/silver and the cash pile's optionality, even though oil's spot reaction has stayed muted so far.

items.headline: Wall Street closes at fresh records Monday as AI mega-caps shrug off 5.3% 10-year yield
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.66% to 7,773.95 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.05% to a record 27,477.31 Monday, led by SpaceX (+7%) plus Nvidia and Tesla (+2% each), even as the 10-year Treasury yield held near a 24-year high around 5.3%. VIX ticked up only marginally to 15.52 from Friday's 15.31, suggesting the rally wasn't accompanied by meaningful hedging demand.
items.actionable: A broad risk-on tape with a still-low VIX argues against chasing near-term fear in the HK-tech/miner book, but elevated yields keep capping upside for the rate-sensitive SGX REIT sleeve.

items.headline: Oil slides despite Gulf escalation as G7's 100M-barrel diesel/crude release works through the market
items.summary: WTI fell 2.05% to $89.24 and Brent 0.92% to $101.31 Monday -- both lower even as the Yemen offensive and Hormuz tensions intensified -- with USO down 2.29%. The G7's Oct 2 agreement, made under US pressure, to release up to 100M barrels of diesel/crude reserves over four months (front-loaded in the first 20 days) is capping prices, though Goldman Sachs estimates it can only offset about half the diesel price surge given Hormuz disruption and Russian export curbs.
items.actionable: The G7 release is a structural lid on how far oil can spike on Gulf headlines -- don't expect a clean follow-through rally in energy-linked inflation trades even if Yemen/Hormuz escalates further.

items.headline: Silver bounces off golden-pocket support to ~$61.72 while gold and miner ETFs stay in the red
items.summary: Spot/futures silver rallied to roughly $61.72/oz Monday (SLV +0.71%) after closing Friday at $60.37, while GLD slipped 0.16% and the levered miner complex (GDX -0.41%, SILJ -0.44%) extended its two-week drawdown. The bifurcation suggests dip-buyers are targeting silver specifically rather than the metals complex broadly.
items.actionable: Silver's bounce off the "golden pocket" is a more encouraging signal than the still-soft miner ETFs -- a futures close back above $60 is the level to watch before adding to SILJ/GDX.

items.headline: HK tech and chip names rebound Monday, reversing Thursday's selloff; Hang Seng +0.28%
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index rose 0.28% to 24,040.34 Monday, with Tencent up 0.43% and SMIC up 1.74% as semiconductor and AI-application names led the recovery; Xiaomi lagged, down 1.49%. The index is still clawing back the 2.6% single-day drop from Friday's post-holiday reopen.
items.actionable: SMIC's chip-led bounce is the more constructive signal for the HK tech sleeve than Tencent/Xiaomi's muted moves -- liquidity stays thin until mainland Stock Connect flows resume Thursday.

items.headline: Mainland China markets and Stock Connect remain shut for Golden Week until Thursday Oct 8
items.summary: China's Golden Week holiday keeps the SSE Composite parked at its pre-holiday 3,842.19 level and Stock Connect (northbound and southbound) suspended through Wednesday Oct 7, resuming Thursday Oct 8. HK-listed China names are trading offshore-only in the interim, raising the risk of a catch-up adjustment once mainland flows return.
items.actionable: Treat this week's HK tech price action as thinner and less reliable than normal -- size any moves with the knowledge that Thursday's Stock Connect reopen could trigger a repricing either way.

items.headline: MP Materials set to deliver GM's first rare-earth magnets made outside China in Q4
items.summary: MP Materials is preparing to ship commercial volumes of rare-earth magnets to General Motors from its 250,000-sq-ft Independence facility in Fort Worth in Q4 2026, after delivering qualification-test magnets in Q2. The milestone follows the Pentagon's $400M, 15% equity stake in MP and a 10-year, $110/kg offtake agreement underpinning the build-out.
items.actionable: A real commercial shipment -- not just a pilot -- to a marquee automaker is the kind of concrete de-risking event the rare-earth watchlist has been waiting for, a positive company-specific data point within the broader China-dependency thesis.

items.headline: FOMC September minutes due Wednesday, with Bowman-Schmid rate-path rift front and center
items.summary: Minutes from the Fed's September meeting are due Wednesday Oct 7 at 2pm ET (pre-dawn Thursday SGT), the week's key macro catalyst. Vice Chair Bowman has said she's pencilled in three rate cuts before year-end on labor-market concerns, while Kansas City's Schmid has favored holding rates given inflation he still views as too high and policy he doesn't see as very restrictive -- the minutes should reveal how wide that split runs across the full committee.
items.actionable: A minutes read showing more hawkish dissent than expected would pressure gold/silver and SGX REITs via higher-for-longer yields; a dovish-leaning committee would support the precious-metals complex into year-end.

items.headline: Bitcoin pops toward 8-month high near $87k before fading back to ~$86,189
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly touched close to $87,000 early Monday -- near an eight-month high -- before reversing to trade around $86,189, still roughly 32% below its prior cycle high near $126,080. Ethereum traded firmer near $2,720 (+1.5% versus Sunday) ahead of the "Glamsterdam" testnet upgrade.
items.actionable: No direct portfolio exposure, but the fade from the intraday high is a reminder that broader risk appetite is still fragile even during a record-setting equity session -- a cross-check on how much of Monday's rally was genuine conviction versus momentum.

items.headline: Hormuz-transiting tanker charter rates surge to ~$1.3M/day, 43x January levels
items.summary: War-risk and charter rates for tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz have climbed to roughly $1.3 million a day -- 43 times January levels -- as the disruption to the strait drags into an eighth month, even as benchmark crude prices themselves have pulled back on the G7 reserve release.
items.actionable: The freight-cost blowout shows the Gulf disruption's economic damage is still intensifying beneath a calmer headline oil price -- a reason to keep the gold/silver hedge rather than read the flat spot price as an all-clear.

items.headline: CapitaLand China Trust retains five-star GRESB rating as shares slip to S$0.61
items.summary: CapitaLand China Trust (CLCT) retained a five-star rating in the 2026 GRESB real estate sustainability assessment, ranking first in its peer group, even as the stock slipped 1.6% to S$0.61 on Oct 2 -- S$0.21 below its 52-week high. DBS maintained a Hold rating with a S$0.65 target; next earnings are due Oct 23.
items.actionable: The sustainability rating is a positive but non-market-moving data point -- the real catalyst for the SGX China-REIT sleeve is the Oct 23 earnings print, worth calendaring.

items.headline: Blackstone Singapore chairman Gautam Banerjee joins DBS boards
items.summary: DBS appointed Gautam Banerjee -- Blackstone Singapore chairman and a sitting director of Singtel and GIC -- to its group and bank boards effective Oct 1, 2026. DBS shares closed around S$77.83 on Oct 5, about 1.5% below their 52-week high, with market cap near S$220.8bn after a 9% y/y rise in Q2 net profit to S$3.1bn.
items.actionable: A well-connected board addition is a minor governance positive for DBS, not a trading catalyst -- the stock's proximity to its 52-week high is the more relevant signal for the core SG-bank holding.
